description: How long a credential stays valid, whether it is a cookie or a signed token, and -- on the JavaScript side -- a window opened without cutting the reference back to the page that opened it. Both negatives are the discriminators: a preference cookie that lasts a year is a feature, and a lifetime is only long relative to the unit the call counts in.

expected.note: a year; the fifteen-minute cookie below and the year-long THEME cookie are both silent, and for different reasons
no third argument, which is where noopener would be; the call below has one

an ABSENCE: the options were enumerated and expiresIn is not among them. A signed token carries no revocation of its own, so unless the server keeps state to check it against, its expiry is the only thing that ends it
